problemStatement.formal: For d > 0: (not IsConstructible alpha d) iff not (exists k, d = 2^k). Equivalently, d has an odd prime factor iff degree d is non-constructible.
problemStatement.plain: A degree d guarantees non-constructibility if and only if d has an odd prime factor. The constructible degrees are exactly the powers of 2.
whyMatters: Provides the complete number-theoretic characterization underlying Wantzel's theorem
Explains WHY degree 3 is the obstruction (not just that it is)
Extends naturally to regular polygon constructibility (Gauss-Wantzel theorem)
Connects to Fermat primes and the classification of constructible n-gons

proven: prime_dvd_pow_two_eq_two - any prime factor of 2^n must equal 2
odd_prime_dvd_not_dvd_pow_two - odd prime factor prevents dividing 2^n
dvd_pow_two_is_pow_two - divisors of 2^n are powers of 2 (strong induction)
dvd_pow_two_iff - complete characterization: d | 2^n iff d = 2^k
not_constructible_of_odd_prime_factor - odd prime factor implies non-constructible
constructible_degree_is_power_of_two - constructible degree must be power of 2
Complete regular n-gon constructibility for n=3..20 (11 constructible, 7 not)
